entities.name: Chloropyridine nitrile
observations: Standardized substrate: Cc1cc(C)c(C#N)c(Cl)n1; an activated methyl-substituted chloropyridine bearing an aryl nitrile and heteroaryl C–Cl bond.
The C–Cl site is a leaving-group handle for nucleophilic aromatic substitution, not an imidoyl chloride.

entities.name: Methoxy pyridine nitrile
observations: Standardized product: COc1nc(C)cc(C)c1C#N; methoxy replaces the substrate chlorine.

entities.name: Sodium methoxide
observations: The closest exact database record uses sodium methoxide, CH3O− with Na+, to convert the chloropyridine substrate to the methoxy product.

entities.name: Chloropyridine methoxylation
observations: Nucleophilic aromatic substitution of activated heteroaryl chloride by methoxide gives the corresponding methoxypyridine nitrile.
Neutral methanol alone is less reactive; methoxide-generating base or preformed sodium methoxide is more plausible.

entities.name: Methanolic sodium methoxide
observations: Plausible practical formulation: sodium methoxide in methanol, with heating or reflux as needed. The returned exact record did not specify temperature or time.
